_comment: REAL prices, read from the LiteLLM gateway the fleet actually bills through. Source: GET https://llm.megabyte.space/v1/model/info (litellm_params.input_cost_per_token / output_cost_per_token / cache_read_input_token_cost), fetched 2026-11-18. Route mapping at that time: deepseek-v4-pro -> deepseek/deepseek-reasoner, deepseek-flash -> deepseek/deepseek-chat. Re-fetch before quoting any figure; this file is a dated snapshot, not a live rate card.
_warning: deepseek-v4-pro and deepseek-flash currently bill at the SAME per-token rate. Tier routing therefore saves $0.00 on rate. The routing benefit is latency plus lower output volume; the dollar saving comes from prompt-cache hits. Do not claim routing-driven percentage savings at these rates.

_measurement.pro_output_multiplier: Measured 2026-11-18 through the same gateway: fixed code-review task, max_tokens=600, temperature=0, 3 samples per model. deepseek-flash completion tokens 85/52/52; deepseek-v4-pro completion tokens 600/600/600 (588-600 of them reasoning_tokens, finish_reason=length, empty content). 600/85 = 7.06, so 7.1 is a LOWER BOUND on the Pro/Flash output-token ratio for that task: Pro was truncated and still billed the full 600. Re-measure on a longer-output task before treating this as converged.
_measurement.cache_hit: Measured 2026-11-18: 10,511-char system prompt, 6 sequential identical calls per model. Cache hit tokens 2432/2629 (92.5%) for deepseek-flash and deepseek-chat, 2432/2654 (91.6%) for deepseek-v4-pro; 6/6 calls hit after the first. The issue's 91% assumption holds in this environment.
